Scale: 1,067 sessions · 53,362 attributed contributions (47,290 spoken in the chamber, 6,072 submitted in writing) · 2,473 identified persons · 76 years of proceedings Why this chamber is different The Bundesrat is not a second elected chamber. Its members are delegates of the sixteen Land governments, appointed and recallable by them. Article 51(3) of the Basic Law requires each Land to cast its votes einheitlich as a bloc and the chamber has no Fraktionen (no party affiliations).
There is therefore no party field, and its absence is a design decision rather than a gap: the operative political unit is territorial. Every contribution carries the Bundesland it was made for, which makes territorial representation and federal–state conflict directly measurable from text. The chamber is also permanent, never dissolved, no elections, continuous session numbering since 1949 so the corpus is a single unbroken series rather than one segmented by legislative period.
Dataset files speeches.parquet, one row per attributed contribution by a named member: speaker name, resolved person_id, role, Bundesland, full German text, and contribution_type marking whether it was spoken in the chamber or submitted to the record in writing (102 MB). Gender is not stored here; join persons.parquet on person_id. persons.parquet, one row per resolved individual: canonical name, all name variants merged, career span, modal role and Bundesland, gender. Use this, not speakers.parquet, for person-level analysis.
sessions.parquet, one row per sitting: date, meeting city, extraction engine, source PDF hash, presiding_land (the Land holding the rotating annual presidency), and separate counts of spoken and written contributions. speakers.parquet, name-string index: one row per unique name string as extracted. Useful for assessing extraction quality; not suitable for person-level aggregation. laender.csv, reference table resolving the 19 values the land field can take, with observed first and last year

# The Bundesrat corpus: A dataset of political discourse in the German Federal Council
## 1 Background & Summary
To address the aforementioned data gap, in this Data Descriptor, we present a complete speaker-attributed corpus of 1,067 Bundesrat plenary sessions from the chamber’s first sitting on 7 September 1949 to 10 July 2026. It comprises 53,362 speeches delivered in the chamber including written statements.
## 2 Methods
### 2.2 Data Source
It is published in different period-based web pages (e.g., 1949–1950, 1951–1955, …, 2026–2030) as PDF documents. Each PDF document represents one session and the filename carries useful information, including session number and date that are essential for building the metadata. The corpus is designed to be extensible; thus, newer sessions can be added accordingly.
## 3 Data Records
### 3.1 Dataset Overview
The dataset contains four tables built from 1,067 per session attribution files and the extraction catalog by a packaging step that performs no parsing of its own. Every field in the corpus is either carried from the attribution files or computed by aggregation so the package can be built at any time without disturbing the speech layer.
All text fields are UTF-8 encoded, null values are represented as null in Parquet and as empty strings in the CSV file. The dataset is publicly available on Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/22086439 under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY4.0).

Structured, speaker-attributed corpus of all German Bundesrat (Federal Council) plenary session transcripts (Plenarprotokolle) from the chamber's first sitting to the present (sessions 1–1067, September 1949 – July 2026).
